title: Lesson 2: First Notes, First Chords
intro: This lesson covers the physical basics: how to sit, how to press a string so it rings, how to pick and strum, and how to change between two chords in time. Go slowly: clean notes now save months later.

items: Hold the guitar and fret a clean note.
Pick single notes with alternate picking.
Strum a steady pattern.
Change between two chords in time.
A tuned guitar (Lesson 1), a medium pick, and a metronome (a free app, or set the tempo slider on the fretboard below).
Step 1. Sit with the guitar's waist on your right leg (left leg if you play left-handed), the neck angled slightly up. Keep your back straight and the guitar close to your body.
Step 2. Put your fretting-hand thumb behind the neck, roughly behind your middle finger. Curve your fingers so you press with the very tips.
Step 3. Press string 1 just behind fret 3 (on the headstock side of the fret wire, not on top of it). Pick the string. You should hear a clear G.
Step 4. If it buzzes, move your fingertip closer to the fret or press a little harder. If it sounds dull, part of another finger is touching the string.
Step 5. Now play frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on string 1 with fingers 1, 2, 3 and 4: one finger per fret. This hand position, called first position, is where most beginner music lives.

widget.title: One finger per fret on string 1

items: Step 1. Hold the pick between your thumb and the side of your index finger, with only the tip showing.
Step 2. Pick downward (toward the floor) on the beat and upward between beats: down–up–down–up. This is alternate picking, and it keeps your timing even.
Step 3. Play the exercise below on each string: frets 1-2-3-4, alternating down and up strokes, at a slow, steady tempo (60 BPM). Speed comes later.

widget.title: Chromatic exercise across all six strings (frets 1–4)

items: Step 1. Form an E minor chord (022000): middle finger on string 5 fret 2, ring finger on string 4 fret 2. It is the easiest full chord.
Step 2. Strum down across all six strings with a relaxed wrist. Count '1, 2, 3, 4' and strum on each count.

Step 3. Now keep your hand moving down and up continuously in eighth notes, and hit the strings on 'down–down up–up down up' (the D–D U–U D U pattern): down on 1, down on 2, up on 'and', miss on 3, up on 'and', down on 4, up on 'and'. The hand never stops; it only misses some strokes.
Step 4. Step through the strum below and copy it.

widget.title: Em with the D – D U – U D U pattern

items: Step 1. Play E minor (022000), then A minor (x02210): fingers 2 and 3 move across one string each, and finger 1 goes onto string 2 fret 1.
Step 2. Practise the change without strumming: lift, move, place, ten times. Watch for the finger that moves least and keep it as an anchor.
Step 3. Now strum each chord four times (one bar), then change. If the change makes you late, strum the last beat of each bar on the open strings to give your hand time.
Step 4. Add a third chord, C (x32010): from Am, only finger 3 moves (from string 3 fret 2 to string 5 fret 3). Then G (320003).

widget.title: Em – Am – C – G, one bar each

blocks.text: Expressive techniques (come back to these later)

items: Hammer-on: pick a note, then bring another finger down hard on a higher fret of the same string so it sounds without picking. Pull-off: the reverse, flicking the finger off the string as you lift it.
Slide: pick a note and move the finger along the string to another fret, keeping pressure.
Bend: push the string across the fret (usually upward) to raise its pitch, often by a whole step (two frets' worth). Check by playing the target note two frets up first.
Vibrato: a small, quick, repeated bend and release on a held note.
Palm muting: rest the edge of your picking hand on the strings right by the bridge for a short, chunky sound.
Natural harmonics: touch (do not press) a string right above the 12th fret wire and pick it: a bell-like note an octave up. Over fret 7 you get an octave and a fifth; over fret 5, two octaves.

widget.title: Pitches of the harmonics on the low E string (the dots show where these pitches are fretted, not where to touch)

items: 3 min: one finger per fret on every string, alternate picking, metronome at 60.
4 min: Em ↔ Am changes, four strums each, then Am ↔ C, then C ↔ G.
4 min: the D – D U – U D U strum on Em – Am – C – G, at a tempo where you never stop.
2 min: natural harmonics at frets 12, 7 and 5 on each string.

blocks.title: Buzz
blocks.text: A fretted note buzzes. Name two likely causes.
solution: The fingertip is too far from the fret wire (press just behind it), or not pressing firmly enough; also possible: the finger is on top of the fret wire.
blocks.answer: Finger too far from the fret, or too little pressure

blocks.title: Harmonics
blocks.text: Touching the low E string (E2) lightly over the 7th fret gives which pitch?
solution: The 7th fret divides the string into thirds, so it sounds the 3rd harmonic: 3 × 82.4 Hz = 247.2 Hz, which is B3.

blocks.text: Sources: Denyer, R. (1992). The Guitar Handbook, rev. ed. Knopf; Leavitt, W. G. (1966–1971). A Modern Method for Guitar, vols. 1–3. Berklee Press; Noad, F. (2008). Solo Guitar Playing, 4th ed. Schirmer.
